patch.objective: Collect unique values in a set, add and remove members, and test membership
secondaryObjectives: Modify, search and sort a list with append, insert, index, del, sort and sorted, and say which return None

sources.cite: Python Institute, PCEP-30-03 exam syllabus (revised November 2, 2026)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch: Section 03 Data Collections (26%); 3.3.1 'Explain the defining characteristics of the set data type' and 'Test membership using the in and not in operators'; 3.1.2 'Use the in and not in operators to test list membership'. The case: the same membership test against a list inside a loop makes a report take 95 minutes; testing membership in a set makes it 3, measured first and checked against a known good output.

sources.cite: pstats -- Statistics for profilers, Python documentation (3.16 development version)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-16. Relevant text: SortKey.CUMULATIVE, 'Sort by cumulative time'; SortKey.TIME, 'Sort by internal time (time in function excluding subcalls)'; 'All sorts on statistics are in descending order (most time consuming first)'. The column definitions (ncalls, tottime, cumtime) were not on the fetched text; the case uses them as the pstats report labels them.

sources.cite: profile -- Pure Python profiler, Python 3.15 documentation
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-16. Relevant text: 'The cProfile module remains available as a backward-compatible alias to profiling.tracing. Existing code using import cProfile will continue to work without modification'; the example sorts a Stats object by SortKey.CUMULATIVE. The case uses python -m cProfile -s cumulative, which is the long-standing command line.
